business_scope.primary_industry_name: Multi-Parameter Bedside Telemetry Monitor Assembly and Calibration

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (national, unitary jurisdiction; no sub-state tax autonomy)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic) with commercial codification and statutoryization of private-law vehicles; the Private Interest Foundation derives from Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (as amended) and operates as a sui generis hybrid foundation-corporate vehicle.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 31 October 2012); investment chapter protections.
Panama–Canada Free Trade Agreement (in force 1 April 2013); investment chapter protections.
Panama–United Kingdom Double Taxation Arrangement / investment-protection framework for qualifying UK resident investors.
Panama–Netherlands Double Taxation Agreement applicable to treaty-resident Dutch investors and lenders.

Panama–Spain Double Taxation Agreement applicable to treaty-resident Spanish investors; investor-specific treaty eligibility must be confirmed based on tax residence and competent-authority interpretation.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations (Fundaciones de Interés Privado), as amended by Law No. 12 of 2012; Law No. 23 of 27 April 2015 on prevention of money laundering and terrorism financing (AML/CFT), as amended; Law No. 196 of 2021 creating the Panama Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) register, with the UBO disclosure threshold set at 10% ownership, voting rights, or control by other means, and not the 25% FATF-generic default. Implementing authority rests with the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation charter (Escritura Pública de Fundación / Deed of Foundation), including initial capital statement and founder instructions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian Notary Public upon execution by the founder and resident agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Panamanian public instrument; certified copies issued by the Registro Público de Panamá require Apostille by the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores if used abroad; if foreign founder signs abroad, prior notarization and Apostille / Panamanian Consular Legalization in origin will apply

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Written power of attorney (Poder General) in favor of the Panamanian resident agent or formation attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin of the grantor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the origin country is an Apostille Contracting State; otherwise Panamanian Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passport and proof of residential address for each founder, foundation council member, protector, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notarial or governmental authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Apostille or Panamanian Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Legal Existence for each corporate founder (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The applicable companies registry in the corporate founder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille by the home jurisdiction's competent authority, or Panamanian Consular Legalization if the home state is not an Apostille party

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended by Law No. 41 of 1995, Law No. 63 of 2018, and Articles 5, 6, 12, 19, and 21 of the Foundation Regulation under the Public Registry of Panama
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundation Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (Public Deed of Incorporation of Private Interest Foundation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the founder must allocate an initial patrimony of at least US$10,000 or its equivalent. No escrow deposit is required under Panamanian law; the Public Registry accepts a notarial statement of the contributed assets as sufficient proof of patrimony.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The subscription of the initial foundation patrimony is hereby approved, and the Secretary shall evidence receipt of assets valued at not less than US$10,000 as contributed by the Founder; (2) The registered office of the Foundation shall be established at the offices of the Resident Agent in Panama City, Republic of Panama, with legal domicile as stated in the Foundation Charter; (3) The Founder ratifies the appointment of the Foundation Council as the governing body, and the Council hereby appoints the President, Secretary, and Treasurer as named in the Charter; (4) The Resident Agent and all officers are authorized to execute documents and take all actions necessary for registration and lawful commencement of the Foundation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Dirección General de Registro de Fundaciones (online and in-person window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request to the Public Registry via the official online portal or in-person window. The request must include the proposed foundation name (must contain 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or the suffix 'PIF') and the identification data of the founder. No notarization is required at this pre-filing stage.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request form
Copy of founder identification document (passport or national ID)
Scanned copy of the proposed foundation charter excerpt showing the name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or reserved for another entity, the applicant may file a reconsideration petition with the Public Registry within 10 business days, together with three alternative names for immediate re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of the Foundation Public Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de la República de Panamá (certified notary for the jurisdiction of Panama City)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder's Panamanian attorney drafts the Foundation Charter (Estatuto) in Spanish, which must include the foundation purpose, patrimony, council members, beneficiary provisions, registered office, and resident agent appointment. The document is converted into a public deed and signed by the founder and witnesses before the notary. The notary authenticates the signatures and issues a certified copy for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Foundation Charter (Escritura de Fundación)
Notarized attendance and consent of the founder
Acceptance letter of the resident agent
Council member identification documents
Proof of initial patrimony contribution (bank certificate or notarial asset declaration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal defects or contradictory clauses, the attorney will amend the charter by way of a supplementary public deed and renotarize the corrected instrument before submission to the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Foundation Deed with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the certified copy of the notarized public deed to the Public Registry along with the official application for registration (solicitud de inscripción). The Registry examiner verifies legal compliance, including the name, patrimony, representative designation, and resident agent appointment. Upon approval, the foundation is legally incorporated and assigned a unique CDI number (Certificado de Inscripción).
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the public deed
Completed registry application form (acuerdo de inscripción)
Payment receipt of the official filing fee
Power of attorney of the submitting legal representative (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a querella (court challenge) or a notice of observations, the applicant must respond with technical clarifications and supporting exhibits within 30 days, or if the defect is a document gap, the attorney will execute a correction deed and request re-examination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Foundation Charter and Appointment Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Certifications and Delivery Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the incorporation entry is recorded, the Registry issues two certified documents: (i) the Inscripción de la Fundación (registration certificate) and (ii) the first certified copy of the Foundation Charter. The Resident Agent acknowledges the registered office and the Council members in writing. The certificate is the formal proof of legal existence and is used to open bank accounts, acquire assets, and sign contracts.
required_dossiers: Filing receipt from the Public Registry
Certified copy of the reserved name certificate
Resident agent acceptance form
Council member appointment minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains discrepancies in the foundation name, CDI number, or council members, the Resident Agent must apply for a certificate of correction (certificación de rectificación) with supporting corroborative documents and the original deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Impuestos Internos (DGI) and Dirección Nacional de Registro de Fundaciones (internal registry window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the DGI for the foundation's Cédula de Registro Único (tax identification number). The DGI will classify the foundation under the territorial scope. Simultaneously, the foundation must enroll in the annual flat tax registry (annual US$300) and, if applicable, obtain a local municipal operating permit. The tax registration is mandatory for any asset holding, bank account, or real estate transaction.
required_dossiers: Registration certificate (Inscripción de la Fundación)
Certified copy of the Foundation Charter
Resident agent identification
DGI Form 010 (taxpayer registration)
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI rejects the application due to missing documentation or incomplete filing, the applicant will be notified in writing. The resident agent must supply the missing documents, correct the tax form, and re-file the application within 15 business days; no penalty is assessed if corrected before the first annual tax deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI), Dirección General de Industrias
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia Industrial de Funcionamiento (Industrial Operating License) and Aviso de Operación for manufacturing and calibration facilities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAmbiente), Dirección de Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I – Registro de Impacto Ambiental (low-impact environmental registration) because the activity is assembly, calibration, and light electronics manufacturing, non-extractive and low-polluting
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet national effluent standards under Decreto Ejecutivo No. 23 de 2014: pH 6.0–9.0, total suspended solids ≤ 35 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 50 mg/L, COD ≤ 100 mg/L; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions must be controlled to below 50 mg/m³ at stack discharge point as per Resolution AG-0358-2016 and the applicable atmospheric emission inventory limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de la República de Panamá; structural load inspection certificate issued by a registered civil engineer and submitted to the municipal building authority; occupational health and workplace clearance certificate from the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) covering ergonomics, electrical safety, and medical device assembly hygiene.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama. Primary e-Tax portal: 'Sede Electrónica de la DGI' at https://sede.dgi.gob.pa ; institutional website: https://www.dgi.gob.pa . The RUC and ITBMS registration, SIFEL electronic invoicing, monthly returns, and export zero-rating controls are administered exclusively through this portal and the SIGA customs platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must follow a five-step national tax registration procedure. Step 1: Execute the notarized foundation charter (Acta de Fundación) before a Panamanian Notary through a licensed resident agent (abogado idóneo) and endow the foundation with its statutory initial patrimony; Panama's Law 25 of 1995 does not fix a statutory minimum capital amount, but the charter must identify an initial patrimony and practice commonly uses at least B/.10,000 (Balboa/USD at parity). Step 2: Inscribe the PIF in the Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry, Mercantile Section) to obtain the juridical-person certificate, which is the pre-requisite for any tax registration. Step 3: File the DGI 'Solicitud de Registro Único de Contribuyente' together with the registered foundation deed, resident-agent evidence, and the economic activity code (ISIC 3250) to obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente); the RUC is the single statutory tax identifier used for income tax, ITBMS, municipal operating permits, customs declarations, and export documentation. Step 4: Register as an ordinary ITBMS taxable person (contribuyente) because the PIF will perform taxable transfers (assembly and sale of ECG patient monitors) in Panama; there is no separate VAT ID — the RUC includes the ITBMS registration. Step 5: Apply to the DGI for SIFEL electronic-invoicing authorization, obtain the digital signature certificate, and, if components are imported, register as an importer/exporter in the SIGA customs system. A PIF whose activities are purely passive and foreign-source may remain a non-active RUC holder, but active manufacturing and sales require full registration, monthly ITBMS returns, and annual income-tax filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama applies a territorial income-tax system. A Private Interest Foundation is a juridical person for all Panamanian tax purposes and is taxable at entity level only on Panama-source income; foreign-source income and foreign capital gains are outside the domestic tax net. Panama does not operate a domestic 'check-the-box' or pass-through election: the PIF is never fiscally transparent under the Código Fiscal. No hybrid-mismatch election is available under Panamanian domestic law, and classification conflicts arising abroad (for example, an IRS Form 8832 election treating the PIF as a disregarded entity for U.S. federal income tax) have no effect on the PIF's Panamanian territorial classification. Commercial elective regimes conferring tax treatment — the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime and the Colon Free Zone license — require separate DGI/MICI approval and do not alter the territorial-tax characterization. The only directly available elective simplification is the small-taxpayer ITBMS quota, available while annual gross receipts remain within the statutory ceiling.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — Panamanian VAT/GST levied on the transfer, sale, and importation of goods and the rendering of services in Panama; exports of goods and qualifying offshore services are zero-rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary registration exemption: under the ITBMS provisions of the Código Fiscal (Arts. 1052-A et seq.), every person that habitually sells goods or renders services in Panama, or imports goods, must register as an ITBMS taxpayer from the first taxable transaction, regardless of turnover volume. An optional Simplified Taxpayer Regime is available to small vendors whose annual gross taxable revenue does not exceed B/.36,000 (Panama Balboa at 1:1 parity with the U.S. dollar, which is the circulating currency); such taxpayers substitute the ordinary monthly ITBMS return for a fixed periodic quota. Exceeding the B/.36,000 threshold, or commencing regular import or export operations, immediately triggers ordinary ITBMS registration and monthly filing obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory under the DGI's SIFEL electronic-invoicing system (Resolution 201-6004 of 2019, as amended). Active RUC holders carrying on taxable activities must: (1) hold a DGI-validated digital signature certificate (firma electrónica); (2) generate each sales invoice, credit note, and debit note as an XML document in the prescribed DGI schema; (3) transmit the XML to the DGI validation web service (SOAP/REST API with PKI authentication) in near-real-time — administratively interpreted as no later than 24 hours from issuance — and receive the DGI 'acuse de recibo' with a validation code; (4) reflect the validation code and a QR-type digital stamp on the customer-facing invoice; and (5) submit the monthly ITBMS return (Form 184) reconciling SIFEL-issued invoices, export invoices, and input VAT credits. Export invoices must identify the transaction as an export and must be linked to the SIGA customs export declaration so that the DGI can automatically cross-match invoicing, customs exit, and bank receipt data for zero-rating verification.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% ITBMS rate is available for: (1) definitive exports of Panamanian-manufactured goods — including multi-parameter bedside telemetry monitors and ECG devices — where the goods physically leave Panamanian customs territory under a SIGA export declaration and title passes to a foreign buyer; (2) services supplied from Panama to non-resident persons for use and benefit wholly outside Panama, such as offshore calibration, installation, and telemetry-support services invoiced to foreign hospitals, provided no economic use occurs in Panama; and (3) sales to licensed Colon Free Zone or special economic zone operators, subject to strict zone documentation. The exporter must hold an active RUC/ITBMS registration, must issue the export invoice in SIFEL export format, and must demonstrate the complete documentary chain: customs exit, shipping, and receipt of foreign currency proceeds in a Panamanian bank account. The sale of goods actually delivered and used in Panama, or an incomplete customs exit, is taxed at 7%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación / DEX) validated in the SIGA (Sistema Integrado de Gestión Aduanera) platform
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (airfreight) evidencing physical departure of the consignment from Panama to the foreign consignee
Commercial Export Invoice (Factura de Exportación) issued through SIFEL at 0% ITBMS, showing the exporter's RUC and the referenced SIGA declaration
Inward Remittance Certificate / Bank Credit Confirmation (Certificación Bancaria de Ingreso de Divisas) evidencing the credit of export proceeds to a Panamanian bank account
Packing list and, where applicable, MINSA technical/health clearance or product registration evidence for Class II medical devices (ECG monitors)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI subjects zero-rated exports to documentary fiscalization: the SIFEL export invoice must match the SIGA export declaration, the transport document, and the supporting bank credit. Records must be retained for at least 5 years. Although Panama maintains no exchange-control legislation requiring repatriation, the DGI administratively treats bank receipt of proceeds as probatory; an export recorded without inward crediting within 180 days of shipment is presumptively a domestic taxable sale. In a successful audit challenge the DGI will: reclassify the transaction as taxable, assess 7% ITBMS on the invoice value; add monthly late-payment interest at 1% per month or fraction thereof (Código Fiscal recargo provisions); impose administrative fines (generally from B/.50 to B/.5,000 per infraction, with higher fines for false records); and claw back any input VAT credits generated by the exported production or any refund previously paid, with interest from the date of refund. Fraudulent zero-rating — false export declarations, forged customs or shipping documents, or fictitious inward remittances — triggers penalties up to 100% of the omitted tax, DGI suspension or revocation of SIFEL issuing authorization and exporter status, and criminal prosecution for tax fraud and document falsification, including imprisonment under the Código Fiscal and Código Penal, plus responsible-officer liability and extended assessment periods for concealed fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) — the banking regulator and de facto financial supervisory authority in the absence of a central bank; Banco Nacional de Panamá serves as the State's clearing agent and fiscal agent under the Panamanian Monetary Agreement with the United States.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is fully dollarized: the Panamanian balboa is a non-issued unit of account at par with the US dollar, and the US dollar is legal tender. There are no exchange-control restrictions on current-account or capital-account transactions. Profit remittances, dividend distributions, and capital repatriation may be made freely in USD without prior central-bank authorization, conversion tax, or mandatory exchange rate applied. The only practical hurdles are bank-level documentary checks for source of funds, sanctions screening, and final beneficial owner identification imposed under SBP anti-money laundering rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama imposes no statutory surrender of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no time limit for retaining foreign currency. Export receipts for multi-parameter ECG patient monitors and related ISIC 3250 hardware may be held indefinitely in USD or any currency, and may be used directly for inbound component procurement, trade settlement, or treasury investment at the PIF's discretion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BAC International Bank, Inc. — Panama Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium, with a defensive posture: offshore digital EMI accounts may be used only as auxiliary treasury tools, e.g. for procurement cards or low-value disbursements, after a formal banking relationship is established. Under Panamanian law, only SBP-licensed banks and authorized payment service providers may accept deposits or carry out payment processing from the public; an unlicensed foreign EMI operating as a primary treasury or clearing hub would trigger unauthorized banking activity and AML risk. Therefore SWIFT wire and documentary credit operations must sit with a regulated Panamanian bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance is generally required for the PIF founder and at least one appointed council member for the initial account opening, before a notary or bank officer, with original or apostilled identification and certified foundation documents. Some Tier-1 banks permit fully remote opening only for pre-approved, higher-net-worth applicants using biometric video verification, secure electronic Docusign, apostilled copies, and an existing private-banking relationship. Remote opening is never an automatic statutory right; it remains a bank-specific discretionary facility subject to SBP fitness and propriety review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly registered Private Interest Foundation with nominee council members and no prior audited financial history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit foundational documentation package: original Foundation Charter, certified under the Public Registry of Panama; registered Bylaws; Certificate of Existence; sworn declaration identifying the ultimate beneficial owner; list of foundation council members and their appointments; notarized apostilled passports of council members; signed resolutions conferring signatory authority; certificate of the registered agent/office occupant; bank reference letter from the sponsoring private bank; detailed business narrative covering the ISIC 3250 electronic ECG monitor assembly and distribution model; and an open-source or audited source-of-wealth statement for initial foundation capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity outbound wire traffic to East Asian component suppliers with an apparent mismatch between purchase invoices and physical trade flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a complete trade-file chain for each disbursement: purchase order; proforma invoice; executed commercial contract; UCP600-compliant documentary credit or SWIFT MT103 settlement instruction; commercial invoice; packing list; bill of lading or airway bill; cargo insurance certificate; customs declarations where the goods enter or leave Panama; product technical dossiers such as IEC/ISO certification for patient monitors; supplier KYC profiles; and periodic reconciliation of bank outflows against receivable milestones and inventory records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Application pattern characterized by rapid account activation, request for multi-currency accounts, and Panama tax-haven perceptions historically associated with FATF risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Demonstrate substantive local and commercial reality: a physical or virtual Panamanian office through a licensed registered agent; documented minutes for council resolutions; real trade contracts with named suppliers and customers; SBP-compliant ultimate beneficial owner disclosure; commitment to periodic financial statements prepared by an independent Panamanian CPA; and evidence that treasury flows align with genuine medical device assembly and export operations, including WH/IEC/GMP-style quality records and serialized device data.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound PIF capital and shareholder contributions should be routed as USD-denominated SWIFT MT103 messages from a foreign corporate or personal account into a Panama-based USD account at a Tier-1 correspondent bank. The remittance field 70 should state a clear economic purpose such as 'PIF - Capital Contribution - ISIC 3250 ECG Monitor Trading Operations'. Although Panama imposes no statutory exchange-control filing, the receiving bank will perform normal AML and source-of-funds vetting; therefore the sender should annex the foundation charter, capital resolution, distribution agreements, invoices, and a sworn source-of-wealth declaration. For intra-LatAm flows, CHIPS, Fedwire, or SWIFT via New York correspondents may be used; no mandatory conversion to balboas arises because the balboa exists only as an accounting denomination at parity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 or MT202 COV for TT wire settlements of component purchases, freight, calibration services, and standard operational expenses. For high-value ECG monitor supply contracts, issue a commercial documentary letter of credit under UCP600 with the nominated Panamanian bank as issuing bank, utilizing SWIFT MT700/MT707 instructions; SWIFT MT798 is permissible for LC-related message exchange with long-standing counterparties. The PIF may also use documentary collection (D/P or D/A) for lower-risk repeat suppliers. All outbound disbursements must resolve against the originating invoice, airway bill or bill of lading, inspection certificate, and, where applicable, Panama Customs export/import declarations. Given the Panama/USD monetary system, there is no FX conversion step for USD payments; for non-USD trade denominations, settlement is supported by multi-currency accounts and the hedging instruments below.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot contracts for immediate EUR/CNY/CHF liquidation using SBP-licensed counterparties
Vanilla FX forward contracts, up to 12 months tenor, for committed procurement inflows from Europe and China
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted non-convertible currencies, specifically CNY, executed with a licensed international bank or Panama branch
Cross-currency swaps for medium-term USD/EUR supply-contract obligations and balance-sheet hedging
FX vanilla options for contingent international procurement or unexpected tariff-driven re-invoicing flows
Natural hedging through USD-denominated invoicing and strategic treasury pooling across Panama, US, and regional accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Tax / Franchise Maintenance Fee (Tasa Anual de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Republic of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year; non-extendable but administrative due-dates may be formally rescheduled by DGI resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues a USD 50 surcharge plus monthly interest; the Public Registry withholds certificates of good standing while arrears persist; arrears for two consecutive years can initiate administrative strike-off proceedings and loss of the legal entity's active status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (Confirmación Anual de Beneficiario Final under Law 254 of 2021)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Beneficial Ownership Registry, filed through the Panama registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after the foundation's registration anniversary, and within 30 calendar days after any transfer of foundation interests or change in beneficiaries
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary fines and blocking of subsequent registry filings under Law 254 of 2021; unresolved UBO discrepancies may also cause tax-compliance certificates to be withheld and trigger a DGI information-solicitation proceeding.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada Anual de Renta) if Panamanian-source income or local commercial activity exists
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Republic of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of the year following the fiscal year-end (calendar-year PIF); a passive PIF with no Panama-source income is not required to file a substantive tax return but must keep records sufficient to prove its exempt status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% per month of the tax due (capped at 50%), late-payment interest, and administrative collection remedies; delinquency prevents issuance of a tax-clearance certificate and may expose the foundation to strike-off under the fiscal registry rules.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is imposed on a passive asset-holding Private Interest Foundation. A certified audit becomes mandatory when Panama-source gross revenue exceeds USD 1,000,000 per fiscal year, total assets in Panama exceed USD 3,000,000, or the medical-device/patient-monitor activity is subject to a specific health or tax authority regulatory audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB and adopted in Panama by the Colegio de Contadores Públicos Autorizados de Panamá; IFRS for SMEs is acceptable for a non-publicly accountable foundation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 254 of 2021, the registered agent must maintain a complete and current beneficial-ownership schedule for the foundation. This schedule must be confirmed to the DGI Beneficial Ownership Registry on an annual basis within 30 days of the foundation's registration anniversary. If any share/foundation-interest transfer or substitution of a beneficiary occurs during the year, the foundation council minutes, transfer documentation, and amended foundation deed (if executed) must be entered in the statutory registers and the UBO schedule must be updated within 30 days of the transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors / Foundation Council Members
Minute Book (Actas del Consejo de la Fundación)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 – USD 1,200 per annum typical registered-agent and registered-office retainer for a passive Panama private interest foundation
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 – USD 4,000 per engagement only when an audit threshold is triggered; normally USD 0 for a passive non-operating foundation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation applies; a Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) is exempt from Panamanian corporate income tax on non-Panamanian-source income including foreign passive income, capital gains from offshore assets, and distributions from foreign entities. The PIF bears only the annual flat government fee of USD 300 and registration fees under Law 25 of 1995. If the PIF engages in Panamanian-source commercial activities, the 25% rate applies to net Panamanian-source profits; preferential regimes (e.g., Multinational Headquarters SEM under Law 41/2007, Panama-Pacifico) may reduce effective rates. Manufacturing or calibration of medical devices physically performed in Panama may claim deductions for local payroll, utilities, and depreciation, but no statutory patent-box or R&D super-deduction currently applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 2021 (Declaración Jurada Anual de Impuesto sobre la Renta) filed electronically through the DGI e-Tax portal of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa); quarterly advance income tax payments are submitted through the same virtual system using the advance payment declaración format.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal-year return); quarterly advance income tax payments (anticipos) for taxpayers with Panamanian-source revenue exceeding statutory thresholds.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return due within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year taxpayer, the filing deadline is 15 March of the following year. Quarterly advance payments are due on the last business day of the month following each calendar quarter (April, July, October, January).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 (Renglón 1) – Ingresos Brutos de Fuente Panameña
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross sales, service revenue, assembly fees, calibration fees, and incidental receipts derived from economic activity carried out, exercised, or realized within Panamanian territory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident PIF must report only Panamanian-source gross receipts; foreign-source manufacturing or delivery income under FOB or CIF terms is excluded and should be shown in the exempt/foreign-source lines, not in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 (Renglón 2) – Ingresos Exentos y de Fuente Extranjera
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-Panamanian-source income, passive foreign dividends, interest from offshore banks, gains on disposal of foreign-listed shares, and distributions from foreign subsidiaries or trusts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PIF holding the ECG monitor IP and purchasing finished goods from an affiliate manufacturing site outside Panama must be ready to demonstrate that title transfer, negotiation, and execution of sale contracts occurred outside the Republic of Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 (Renglón 3) – Deducciones Atribuibles a la Renta de Fuente Panameña
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, direct materials, labor, depreciation of fixed assets physically located in Panama, rent, local professional fees, insurance, and other unavoidable expenses exclusively necessary to produce Panamanian-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border management fees, headquarters recharges, and intercompany IP royalties are deductible only if supported by a valid transfer pricing file and tax identification of the payee; undocumented offshore recharges are non-deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 1 minus Box 3, being the net taxable income computed exclusively on Panamanian-source items; losses from foreign-source operations may not offset this balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PIF with no Panamanian-source income reports zero here and may file a nil return; any temporary local activity must be itemized and reconciled with the quarterly advance payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Result of applying the 25% statutory rate to the net taxable income in Box 4. Small taxpayers under the simplified optional regime may apply the applicable flat rate when eligible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs cannot invoke foreign tax credits against Panamanian-source tax; the full 25% is payable, subject only to DTA reductions if the PIF is the treaty resident of a qualified jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 (Renglón 6) – Anticipos y Retenciones a Compensar
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly advance income tax payments previously paid by the taxpayer, plus withholding taxes retained by clients on Panamanian-source invoices paid to the entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs must reconcile all DGI payment receipts; overpayments are creditable against the final annual liability or may be petitioned for refund under Article 718 of the Tax Code.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 (Renglón 7) – Saldo en Favor / Impuesto a Pagar
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Remaining tax liability after offset of Box 6, or the excess credit position where advances exceed the final liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any remaining balance must be paid electronically on or before 15 March; a nil or zero return is acceptable for a PIF that can evidence complete foreign sourcing of all income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a surcharge of 5% of the tax due per month or fraction of a month, capped at 50% of the tax; failure to pay timely accrues default interest at the statutory legal rate plus a 10% delinquency charge; electronic filing violations produce administrative fines of up to USD 100,000 and potential visa/certificate restrictions for taxpayers in arrears.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% withholding on dividends distributed from profits already taxed at the entity level under the territorial system; 10% withholding on dividend-equivalent distributions paid out of exempt or preferentially taxed Panamanian-source earnings. Distributions of foreign-source profits, capital corpus, or PIF patrimony to beneficiaries are beyond the Panamanian territorial nexus and are not subject to withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's DTAs (in force with Singapore, Mexico, Spain, France, Portugal, Netherlands, Qatar, South Korea, and the UAE) apply to Panamanian-source dividends, interest, royalties, and service income. To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident beneficiary must (i) submit a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC/CRT) issued by the treaty counterpart tax authority, apostilled or legalized as required; (ii) provide an OECD-compliant beneficial ownership declaration confirming entitlement to treaty benefits; (iii) deliver the foreign tax identification number; and (iv) request a reduced-withholding authorization from the DGI through the e-Tax portal. No treaty relief is necessary for PIF distributions sourced from foreign assets because such distributions are extraterritorial and untaxed under Panamanian domestic law.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-resident lenders on cross-border loans is free of Panamanian withholding tax under the territorial regime. Royalties and license fees paid to non-residents for intellectual property exploited in Panama are subject to a 12.5% gross-basis withholding tax. Transferor/technical assistance fees may be characterized as royalties when linked to patented or proprietary ECG monitoring technology. Applicable DTA reduced rates range from 5% to 10% for royalties and interest, subject to TRC submission and the beneficial ownership protocol.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 1,000,000 annual aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions (goods, services, royalties, financing, and cost sharing) triggers the mandatory filing of the Panama Transfer Pricing Informative Return (Formulario 2025) and the obligation to prepare and retain the Transfer Pricing Local File under Executive Decree 192 of 2011. The DGI may demand contemporaneous documentation below the threshold when transactions involve non-cooperative jurisdictions, recurring losses, or gross margin anomalies.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Resale Price Method – Precio de Reventa
Cost Plus Method – Coste Más Margen
TNMM – Método del Margen Neto de la Transacción
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not codify Economic Substance Regulations of the BVI/Cayman/UAE model; however, the DGI applies the OECD/BEPS substance-over-form principle and the place of effective management test under Article 6 of the Tax Code. A PIF seeking to be a principal entity or IP owner of ECG monitor supply chains must demonstrate in Panama: physical office or registered agent premises with actual utilization, local bank accounts, its own or contracted full-time qualified staff, board or foundation council minutes evidencing decision-making in Panama, and audited financial records. Absent this substance, the DGI may reclassify the PIF as a sham or `cáscara` vehicle and reassess its worldwide commercial flows as Panamanian-source income, or alternatively deny the penalty reductions available to compliant taxpayers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Mischaracterization of Panamanian-Source Transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A PIF that negotiates, calibrates, assembles, or distributes patient monitoring devices within Panama while invoicing foreign affiliates for offshore commissions to avoid the 25% corporate rate; underreporting local gross receipts; using offshore shell accounts to conceal Panamanian-source cash collections.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the full Panamanian-source income at 25% plus 5% monthly surcharge (up to 50%), legal interest, and a flagship penalty of up to 200% of the evaded tax; criminal conviction under the Tax Code and Criminal Code carries fines and imprisonment of 2 to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Founders, foundation council members, and resident agent signatories who knowingly prepared false declarations face joint and several civil liability for the uncovered tax and penalties; the commercial court may order injunctions, asset seizures, and travel bans pending criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PIF as a pure mailbox entity with no office, no employees, no audited accounts, and no board meetings while claiming foreign-source exclusion of sales of ECG telemetry devices delivered through Panama transit points; or using the PIF to route invoicing without any real logistical, financing, or risk-bearing function.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may apply anti-abuse recharacterization and assess tax on the total profit at 25%, deny the application of the arm's length standard entirely, impose documentation penalties of USD 1,000 per month for each missing transfer pricing record, and reject APAs; the registration of the foundation may be suspended for non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or foundation guardians who allow the entity to be used as a sham risk personal liability for the unpaid corporate taxes of the entity under the doctrine of piercing the veil, plus disqualification from serving as resident agents and monetary penalties of up to USD 50,000; criminal charges for fraudulent insolvency may carry imprisonment of 3 to 6 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Beneficial Ownership Registry Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify or disclose the ultimate beneficial owner, the founder, and the beneficiaries of the PIF to the Panamanian Beneficial Ownership Registry (Law 254 of 2021); failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports through the resident agent; failure to keep client KYC files for the bank accounts and supplier relationships tied to the ECG monitor distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to USD 1,000,000 for the PIF and its resident agent; cancellation of the PIF's inscription in the commercial registry; prohibition from opening or maintaining banking relationships; criminal penalties under Law 23 of 2015 for wilful non-disclosure carry imprisonment of 2 to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members and the registered agent are personally exposed to civil fines, revocation of their agency license, immediate freezing of personal and corporate accounts, and arrest warrants leading to travel restrictions should the registry violations conceal illicit enrichment or sanctioned-party dealings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent Profit Repatriation and Evasion of Dividend-Equivalent Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing Panamanian-source retained profits to a foreign beneficiary as a purported 'corpus distribution' without withholding the 5% or 10% dividend-equivalent tax; disguising royalties or interest as non-taxable capital distributions; issuing a false tax residence certificate to a foreign affiliate to justify a treaty reduction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The distributing PIF is held liable for the unwithheld amount plus a 50% surcharge, interest, and a specific penalty of 100% of the tax evaded when the mischaracterization is found to be intentional; the beneficiary may also be subject to gross-up taxation on the entire distribution;
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Signatories of the foundation council who authorized the disguised repatriation are personally liable for restitution of corporate assets and tax debts; criminal courts may impose sentences of 2 to 4 years, occupational bans for professional directors, and preventive seizure of personal property, yachts, or other luxury assets; travel bans are routinely granted at the DGI's request during pending criminal tax proceedings.
